items.item: Each row shows the user's name and email, role, status in words (such as Active, Invited, Deactivated, Locked) and whether two-factor sign-in is enabled
items.evidence: userRowHtml() renders name, email, role, and statusBadge() (Active/Invited/Deactivated text). No column, icon, or data field anywhere for two-factor/2FA status — not in the table headers (<th>Name/Email/Role/Status/Last sign-in</th>) nor in the user data model (buildUsers() only sets id/name/email/role/status/lastSignIn/isOwner).

items.item: Last sign-in uses one date-time format with the timezone stated, relative times also expose the exact time, and an account that has never signed in shows "Never" rather than a blank or a 1970 date
items.evidence: formatDateTime() = Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-US', {month:'short',day:'numeric',year:'numeric'}) + time, with no timeZoneName option, so no timezone is ever stated (screenshot shows 'Nov 6, 2026, 8:45 AM · yesterday' with no TZ). Relative time does accompany the exact time ('· yesterday'), which passes. But a never-signed-in user renders '—' with sr-only text 'Not set' (userRowHtml: formatEmpty() returns '—', sr-only span says 'Not set'), not the word "Never".

items.item: Users can be found by searching name or email and filtered by role, status and inactivity (such as no sign-in for 90+ days), with the number of matching users shown
items.evidence: Search (matchesSearch over name/email) and role/status filters exist (role-filter-panel, status-tab tablist) and matching count is shown ('Showing 1–25 of 56 users', #result-count-live). However there is no inactivity filter — 'More filters' only exposes a generic #filter-date-from/#filter-date-to 'Last sign-in' date range requiring manual date entry; there is no dedicated inactivity option like a '90+ days inactive' preset, and matchesDate() actually excludes users with null lastSignIn from any date-range filter.

items.item: The invite form requires an email and a role, labels both fields, and shows an inline error for a malformed address or one that already has an account
items.evidence: validateInviteField(): email required + regex /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ check + 'A user with this email already exists.' duplicate check against ALL_USERS; role required ('Select a role.'). Labels: <label for="invite-email">Email *</label> and <label for="invite-role">Role *</label>, with inline #invite-email-error / #invite-role-error shown on blur and on submit.

items.item: Deactivation asks for confirmation that names the user and states the effect (active sessions ended, sign-in blocked, data kept), and a deactivated user is offered Reactivate instead
items.evidence: onDeactivate() opens a confirm dialog titled 'Deactivate account for {u.name}?' (names the user) with description 'They will immediately lose access and all active sessions will end.' — this covers sessions ended and access/sign-in blocked, but never states that data is kept/retained. Reactivate is offered for deactivated users via action-reactivate button ('Reactivate account').

items.item: The signed-in administrator's own row is marked (such as "You") and cannot be deactivated or lose the admin role, and the last remaining administrator cannot be deactivated, with the disabled action explaining why
items.evidence: There is no concept of the signed-in administrator's identity anywhere in state or markup — no 'You' badge or similar. The only special-cased protection is isOwner (user index 0, an arbitrary 'Owner' role) which blocks deactivation via openBlockedDialog('Can’t deactivate {name}', ...), but this is unrelated to 'the signed-in admin' and there is no logic protecting 'the last remaining Administrator' (role==='Administrator') from deactivation or role change.

items.item: Password reset sends a reset link to the user's email address, which the confirmation names, and the administrator never sees, sets or types the new password
items.evidence: onResetPassword(u): showToast('Password reset link sent to ' + u.email + '.'). The toast names the destination email and no password field or value is ever shown/entered anywhere in the dialog/toast flow.

items.item: Row actions are buttons or a keyboard-operable menu whose accessible names include the user (such as "Actions for Mai Nguyen"), and the outcome of an action is announced in an aria-live or role="status" region
items.evidence: row-menu-trigger button has aria-label="Actions for " + escapeHtml(u.name) (e.g. 'Actions for Sophia Bennett'), opens/closes with click and ArrowDown/Enter/Space, menu items navigable with ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Escape. Action outcomes go through showToast(), which creates a div with role="status" (e.g. 'Account deactivated for {name}.').

items.item: A search with no matching users shows a message with a way to clear it, and loading and failed-load states with a retry exist
items.evidence: emptyStateRow('no-results') shows 'No users match “{query}”.' plus a #empty-clear-btn 'Clear filters' button that resets search/filters. Loading: skeletonRows() with tableBody aria-busy="true". Failed load: errorStateRow() shows 'Couldn't load users' with #error-retry-btn wired to onRetry().

notes: Audit.json reports score 100/100 with no automated violations, but several manual checklist items fail: no 2FA indicator, no stated timezone, 'Not set'/'—' instead of 'Never', no dedicated inactivity filter, deactivation copy omits 'data kept', and there is no signed-in-admin self-identification ('You') or last-remaining-administrator protection — only an unrelated 'Owner' (index-0 user) protection exists. No template tells were observed: no gradients, glassmorphism, emoji icons, KPI tiles, uppercase tracked labels, rainbow status colors, oversized radii, or navy/indigo sidebar styling; the sidebar is a plain slate-50/blue-700 scheme and initials avatars are used legitimately for real named users.
